message.content: The viscous friction force depends on the velocity of the body and the coefficient of viscous damping. Damping in a physical pendulum is represented as a torque proportional to the angular velocity. Velocity here refers specifically to the angular velocity of the oscillating system. System models must include this friction term whenever the oscillations are observed to decrease in amplitude over time. Time-dependent amplitude decay signals that the ideal undamped approximation is no longer valid. Valid models of real physical pendulums therefore incorporate the viscous term to capture energy loss.
